problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}a & ∗ \\ b & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $\frac{a}{b}.$
worked_solution:
From the Jordan matrix $J,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=-3.
$$

As a result, the first column of $P$ corresponds to an eigenvector of the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$ 

Now, computing $A-(-3)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-3)I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 5 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ -5 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 0 \\ -5 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{1}=1.$
